contexts.text: The fir, box,etc. = celestial natural things.
The fir () = the truths and goods of the exterior man.
The firs, and the planes () = natural things; firs, natural things as to good, planes, as to truth.
The fir, the pine, and the box () = the corresponding natural goods and truths.
The leaves of the fir, poplar, oak, and pine = rational truths from sensuous light.
The fir, pine, and box = the good and truth thence derived in the Natural... Those things of the Church which are in the natural man, are signified by the fir, pine, and box.
The firs () = the external truths of the Spiritual Church, also from good.
The firs () = the Perceptive of the natural man.
The height of the cedars and the choice of the firs... () = rational and natural truths as to perception.
The fir = higher natural truth; the pine, lower natural truth; and the box, the understanding of good and truth there.
